standard.title: Elements of music across cultures and contexts
standard.description: explore ways that the elements of music are combined in music across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored music for similar purposes across cultures and compared performance and audience expectations (AC9AMU4E01). They can identify how elements are used in a piece and describe purposes. The new demand is specifically on how elements are combined — and on evaluation of personal response and musical preferences using music terminology.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore ways that elements of music are combined in music across cultures, times, places and other contexts, evaluating personal responses and describing how structural features create effects.

nodes.label: How elements are combined in diverse music
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe how multiple elements of music are combined in a piece and identify the effect of those combinations.
nodes.minimum_width: Listen to one piece and describe how at least two elements are combined (e.g. fast tempo with loud dynamics, repeated melodic pattern with changing timbre); name the effect of that combination.
nodes.typical_width: Listen to music with diverse instrumentation, forms and cultural origins; describe how elements are combined across whole works and sections; identify which instruments play melody vs accompaniment; compare original versions with arrangements and covers to explore how changing element combinations changes the effect.
wider: Compare an original version of a song with a cover or arrangement — identify which elements changed, which stayed the same, and how the combination differences change the overall effect
Listen to music from an Asian culture and describe how elements are combined — use music terminology and your own words to explain the effect and your personal response

response_modes.reason: Understanding element combinations is built through encountering many examples. Different genres, styles and cultural traditions use element combinations in distinctly different ways — the range of examples determines how flexible and nuanced students' analytical listening becomes.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Original vs cover comparisons and diverse cultural music examples offer particularly rich analytical opportunities — students can isolate specific element combination changes and trace their effects directly.
success_criteria: Can describe how at least two elements are combined in a piece of music
Can name the effect of those element combinations on the music's mood or meaning

nodes.label: Evaluating personal responses with reasons
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate and share personal preferences for music from diverse contexts, using both their own words and music terminology, and giving reasons.
nodes.minimum_width: Share a preference for or response to one piece of music using at least one music term and give at least one reason grounded in the music.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate and discuss personal preferences across music from multiple contexts — leisure music, ensemble music, music important to family or community, music from specific genres; use music terminology to describe what creates the preference; give reasons grounded in the music's features rather than vague impressions.
wider: Compare preferences for music from two different cultural contexts — discuss what each communicates and why one is preferred, using specific terminology
Evaluate a piece of game or screen music — describe what the music does for the product and whether it succeeds, using element analysis as evidence

response_modes.reason: Personal response becomes analytically meaningful when grounded in specific musical evidence. Build a response framework: 'I like/don't like this piece because [specific musical feature] creates [specific effect]. I know because [what I listened for].' This bridges felt response and analytical observation.

success_criteria: Shares a personal response to a piece using at least one music term
Gives at least one reason grounded in a specific musical feature

nodes.label: Structural features and music in social contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify structural features (riffs, strumming patterns, song forms) and describe how music is used in celebrations, ceremonies or rituals in at least two contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one structural feature (e.g. a riff, a chorus, an ostinato) in a piece and describe its function; identify one way music is used in a celebration or ceremony they know.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and describe structural features across diverse music (riffs, ostinatos, strumming patterns, verse/chorus, theme and variations); explain how these features create effects; explore how music gives structure to celebrations, ceremonies and rituals in different community contexts; demonstrate understanding of popular song form through parody.
wider: Use parody to demonstrate understanding of popular song structure — compose new lyrics to a known song, justify how the structural form was used, and perform the parody
Investigate how music structures a specific ceremony or ritual in two different cultural contexts — compare the role music plays in each

response_modes.reason: This node integrates structural analysis (identifying devices), cultural context (how music functions in community life) and personal application (parody). It brings together the analytical and contextual threads of the descriptor into a demonstration of integrated musical understanding.

success_criteria: Can identify at least one structural feature in a piece of music and describe its function
Can describe how music is used in at least one celebration, ceremony or ritual context
